description: Helps you decide why customers leave and what to do about each reason: it takes your customer segment, business model and current churn rate, and returns a retention playbook with health signals, interventions and an email draft for each churn reason. If you do not know why customers leave, leave the churn reasons out and you get a churn discovery kit instead. Your current interventions and data signals are used when you give them. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of scale_paid_check when you need interventions and email drafts for supplied churn reasons.

available_data_signals.description: What you can track (comma-separated). E.g., 'login frequency, support tickets, SLA attainment, QBR attendance'. Format is text.

business_model.description: Business model affects health score weighting. enterprise_contract is read further from your text when it names services, connectivity or investment. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas_subscription".

churn_reasons.description: Optional: known churn reasons, comma-separated. If you do not know them, leave this blank and you get a churn discovery kit with a framework for finding the reasons. Format is text. For example, "implementation delays and unclear ownership".

cs_team_size.description: CS team capacity affects intervention strategy. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "no_dedicated_cs".

current_churn_rate.description: Current churn rate (e.g., '5%' or '5% monthly'). Format is text.

current_interventions.description: Optional: What retention tactics you already do (listed and compared with the playbook). Format is text. For example, "schedule an exception review with the finance owner".

customer_segment.description: Customer segment to focus on. Format is text. For example, "manufacturers with 200 to 500 employees".

industry.description: Optional: your own company's sector, so the answer uses the usual buyers, measures and objections for what you sell. Leave it out and the tool reads the sector from your other inputs and names what it read. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

product.description: Optional: Your product or company name, used in the title and the email drafts. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

name: retention_playbook
